statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: No. On these facts, 31 U.S.C. § 5324 does not clearly apply because there is no evidence the business acted with the purpose of evading a Bank Secrecy Act reporting requirement (e.g., CTR filing) through structuring or related conduct.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 targets conduct done “for the purpose of evading” Bank Secrecy Act reporting requirements, including (a)(1) causing/attempting to cause a financial institution to fail to file a required report, (a)(2) causing/attempting to cause a financial institution to file a report with a material omission/misstatement, and (a)(3) structuring/assisting in structuring or attempting to structure a transaction to evade reporting. The fact pattern shows multiple transactions (cash, card, ACH), including some cash transactions above $10,000 (e.g., $11,443.16 on 2026-03-15) and one cash transaction near $10,000 ($10,170.79 on 2026-04-20), but it does not identify any required report (such as a CTR), any financial institution involved, any instruction to avoid reporting, any splitting of a single cash amount into multiple sub-$10,000 deposits/withdrawals on the same day, or any attempt to cause non-filing or misreporting. Because § 5324 requires a specific evasive purpose and the facts do not show that intent or a structuring pattern, § 5324 does not clearly apply; at most, the facts are consistent with ordinary cash retail activity. Contiguous phrase in answer and here: “31 U.S.C. § 5324 does”.
